text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Three Iraqi boats attack Kuwaiti patrol boats, Interior Ministry says.
- Six private sector closed firms established in February.
- Newly-formed foreign investment committee holds its first meeting. Kuwait has established a committee to study measures to encourage foreign investments in the Gulf Arab state.
- Kuwait Stock Exchange trade volume falls 31 percent to 135.2 million share on Sunday, prices stable.
- Police officer gets 20 years in prison for robbery.

- Kuwaiti official says Iraq's oil-for-food deal not enough to cover Kuwait's compensation claims. Kuwait has made claims for over $100 billion for losses resulting from Iraq's 1990-91 occupation. Under the oil-for-food deal some of the proceeds from the limited sale of $2 billion worth of Iraqi oil over a renwable six-month period cover food and medicine imports and compensations for 1991 Gulf War losses. Iraq has been under a United Nations trade embargo since 1990.
- Kuwait mourns former defence minister Sheikh Ali Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah. Sheikh Ali died in London on Sunday.
